title: Selfie under the stars
caption: Self-portrait under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A person and a car stand in the Atacama desert beneath a sky crowded with stars, and both throw a shadow onto the ground. The figure is ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek, and the light casting that shadow does not come from the Moon or a lamp. It comes from the bright band of the Milky Way itself.

On a clear night with no Moon, the stars of our own galaxy become almost the only source of light for miles around this remote corner of Chile. Under skies that dark, even the black and brown clouds of molecular gas threaded through the Milky Way stand out against the glow of the stars behind them.
Far off on the horizon sit the four Very Large Telescopes on Cerro Paranal. While the photographer worked, they were busy recording objects inside our galaxy and well beyond it.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with an ordinary camera at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way's dust clouds and the shadow may appear more clearly than they would to someone standing there.

explore: ESO opens its observatories to thousands of visitors each year. Guests can tour the sites, see the instruments used to photograph the sky, and learn about the work of some of the largest ground-based astronomy facilities anywhere on Earth.
alt: A person beside a car in a dark desert under a star-filled sky with the Milky Way, with the Very Large Telescopes on a distant ridge.
